info.title: SRIFT API
info.summary: Zero-config, zero-token P2P E2EE file transfer + chat for any AI agent or automation. Includes a public download tunnel at https://srift.app/d/<token> so recipients need nothing installed.
info.description:
Two API surfaces:

  1. **Local daemon** at `http://127.0.0.1:3822` (recommended for AI agents — fully token-less).
  2. **Public signaling** at `https://srift.app` (used by browser clients).

For AI agents, use the local daemon endpoints (everything under /quick-share, /session/*, /send, /receive, /chat/*, /mcp). Documentation: https://srift.app/AGENTS.md

post.summary: ZERO-INSTALL delivery: ensure session + register file + return a public relay download URL
post.description: Primary entry point for AI agents. If no session is active, creates one, then registers the file for public HTTP download. Returns a `downloadUrl` like `https://srift.app/d/<token>` the recipient can fetch with any HTTP client (browser, `srift get`, wget, curl) — SRIFT install on the recipient side is NOT required. This is a relay link: when it is opened, this daemon streams the bytes on demand through the srift.app relay (pass-through, `Cache-Control: no-store`). Nothing is stored on any server, so the link works only while this daemon (or the process hosting it) runs. `encrypt: true` (or a `password`) makes it end-to-end encrypted with AES-256-GCM; the key is returned in the URL's `#k=` fragment, which is never sent to a server. Without it the link is protected by TLS in transit only. Optional `maxDownloads` and `ttlMs` enforce sharing limits; failed/cancelled downloads do not count against the cap. Tokens survive transient signaler reconnects. Note: requires the local SRIFT daemon (http://127.0.0.1:3822) — filesystem access to `filePath` is not available on the public https://srift.app host. Several files: pass filePaths for one .tar.gz bundle link (default) or bundle:false for one link per path, created in parallel; the response then has links[] and errors[].

filePath.description: Absolute path to a file or folder (folders are sent as .tar.gz). Use this OR filePaths.

maxDownloads.description: Cap after N completed downloads. 0 = unlimited.

ttlMs.description: Auto-expire the link after N milliseconds. 0 = never.

encrypt.description: End-to-end encrypt (AES-256-GCM). The key is carried in the returned URL's #k= fragment and never sent to a server. Default false (TLS in transit only).

password.description: Optional password the recipient must supply (PBKDF2-SHA256, 100,000 iterations). Implies encrypt.

filePaths.description: Several absolute file/folder paths in one call. Use this OR filePath.

bundle.description: With filePaths: true = one .tar.gz link containing everything; false = one link per path, created in parallel.

bundleName.description: With filePaths + bundle: archive name (.tar.gz is added).

exclude.description: Extra glob patterns skipped when packing folders (.git and node_modules always skipped).

get.summary: Public download tunnel — recipient downloads the file via standard HTTP
get.description: Streams the file as a standard HTTP response from the seeder's daemon via the signaler. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="…"` so browsers and `curl -OJ` / `wget --content-disposition` auto-name the file. Supports HTTP Range (`Accept-Ranges: bytes`) for resume. Honours `maxDownloads` and `ttlMs` set at registration time. Concurrent recipients each get an independent parallel stream.

X-SRIFT-Size.description: Total file size in bytes (the body may be streamed without Content-Length)

X-SRIFT-Encrypted.description: SRE1 = end-to-end encrypted payload (decrypt with the #k= key), none = plain

post.summary: Route an encrypted envelope
post.description: Forwarded only if the recipient is online; result is delivered | offline | unconfirmed | rate_limited | invalid. Nothing is stored. Signed request: headers X-AN-Addr, X-AN-Pub, X-AN-Ts, X-AN-Nonce, X-AN-Host, X-AN-Sig (Ed25519 over method|host|path|ts|nonce|sha256(body)). Normally used through the `srift an` CLI or MCP, which handle signing.
